deep.reconstruction:
Folio 122r is not a computation. It is the fair-copy draft of the title and introduction (Inhaltsangabe) of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen', which appeared in Crelle's Journal vol. 54 (1857). Its content, restated:

(a) Method. The paper treats Abelian functions by the method whose principles were laid down in the 1851 Göttingen dissertation ('Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse', footnote 1). The draft says these principles were presented in a slightly altered form in preceding articles of the same journal. These are the companion notes in Crelle 54: on general assumptions and tools, on analysis situs (Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs), and on determining a function by boundary/discontinuity conditions.

(b) Part I, on a system of equally branched algebraic functions on a Riemann surface T and their integrals, without theta series:
- §§1-5: determining such functions by their branching and their singularities (Dirichlet principle, Riemann's existence theorem). Implicitly this includes the count of independent everywhere-finite integrals.
- §§6-10: expressing them rationally in two variables s, z linked by an algebraic equation F(s,z)=0.
- §§11-13: transforming these expressions by rational substitutions. Here the concept of a 'class' of algebraic equations appears: equations transformable into one another by birational substitutions, i.e. a birational equivalence class of curves. §13 treats reduction to equations of lowest degree.
- §§14-16: Abel's addition theorem for any system of everywhere-finite integrals, applied to integrating a system of differential equations, as preparation for Part II.

(c) Part II. For the p everywhere-finite integrals on a (2p+1)-fold connected surface (Riemann's connectivity count for genus p), the Jacobi inversion functions of p variables are expressed by p-fold infinite theta series:
 theta(v_1,...,v_p) = sum over (m_1,...,m_p) in Z^p of exp( sum_{mu,mu'} a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum_mu v_mu m_mu ).
 The convention is a symmetric with negative definite real part (implicit, mine).

(d) Dimension count. For p>3 the thetas needed form a special class. Among the p(p+1)/2 quantities a_{mu mu'} there are (p-2)(p-3)/2 relations, leaving 3p-3 arbitrary. Arithmetic (mine): p(p+1)/2 - (p-2)(p-3)/2 = (p^2+p-p^2+5p-6)/2 = 3p-3. The relation count vanishes for p=2,3, which is consistent with 'p>3'. Riemann adds that this part is also a theory of this special kind of theta function. General thetas are excluded here but can be handled by a similar method.

(e) Priority remark. Weierstrass solved the inversion problem for hyperelliptic integrals in a note (Crelle 47, 1854) and announced properties of hyperelliptic functions.
- Riemann says he thought he should wait for the continuation (extension to the other Abelian functions).
- To keep his theory independent, he avoided using Weierstrass's work and confined himself to stressing the main concepts.
- Footnote 2: the now-published first half of Weierstrass's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 52, 1856) only works out what §§1, 2 and the elliptic-function part of §3 of the 1854 paper had sketched.
errors: No mathematical errors. The dimension count p(p+1)/2 - (p-2)(p-3)/2 = 3p-3 is correct.

The statement that only 3p-3 moduli remain 'arbitrary' is the classical parameter count; it is not a proof of the Schottky-type relations. Riemann gives none, and the relations were only made explicit later (Schottky 1888 for p=4).
'(2p+1)fach zusammenhängend' is Riemann's own connectivity convention for the cut surface of a genus-p surface; it is correct in his terminology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript draft of the published introduction to Riemann's 1857 Crelle paper. Its content, including the 3p-3 count and the remark on Weierstrass, is well known. Only minor wording differences from the printed version could be of philological interest.

checkable.asserts: Number of free theta moduli after the relations equals 3p-3
No relations for p=2,3; one (Schottky) relation for p=4; three for p=5
Codimension of the Jacobian locus in the Siegel space equals (p-2)(p-3)/2

transcription_corrections: 'in den drei Aufsätzen[?] 1[?] ... dieses Journals': the reference is to the companion articles in the same volume of Crelle's Journal (vol. 54). The digits are probably a volume/page reference, not a footnote number.
'Inhaltsangabe' and 'erste Abtheilung' readings are confirmed by the published text, as are the § ranges 1-5, 6-10, 11-13 and 14-16.
'allenthalben endlicher Integrale von gleichverzweigten [-von-] algebraischen Functionen': the struck-through 'von' is correctly marked as deleted.

'in einer Notiz[?] 2)': the footnote marker 2) is attached to Weierstrass's publication (Crelle 47, 1854). The footnote refers to the first half of his 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 52, 1856).

'Die Ausdehnung[?] derselben ... glaubte ich diesen Zwecke[?] abwarten zu müssen' is uncertain. The sense is that Riemann thought he had to await Weierstrass's continuation/extension to the general Abelian functions. 'Fortsetzung' is a plausible reading for 'Ausdehnung'.
'ausgeschlossen[?]' (general theta functions excluded here) fits the sense and is likely correct.
